questions.stem: A patient came to the OPD with complaints of paresis and numbness after sleeping on his arm. Which of the following explains the phenomenon correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: A fibres are more susceptible to pressure than C fibres

options.label: B
options.text: C fibres are more susceptible to pressure than A fibres

options.label: C
options.text: C fibres are more susceptible to hypoxia than A fibres

options.label: D
options.text: B fibres are more susceptible to pressure than A fibres

questions.answerText: A fibres are more susceptible to pressure than C fibres
questions.solutionHtml:
A fibres are more susceptible to pressure than C fibres

A fibres are more susceptible to pressure than B fibers than C fibres.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following event occurs during phase B to raise body temperature to hypothalamus set point?
questions.solutionHtml:
Shivering

In the above scenario, the patient's hypothalamic thermostat has been reset from point B to a higher temperature . The body responds to this change by using certain measures in stage B such as shivering.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page 901-910

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effectively proven way of increasing life span?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease calorie intake by 30%
  • All the given options have been said to delay ageing and improving health by one way or the other.
  • However, decreasing calories by 30 % (fasting or building a calorie deficit) is the only proven way known to effectively increase the life span.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page 109 - 110

questions.stem: True about NET (Neutrophil Extracellular Traps) are all except?

options.label: D
options.text: It is Chromatin with anti-bacterial enzymes

questions.solutionHtml:
Mitochondrial DNA is seen
  • Mitochondrial DNA is not typically seen in Neutrophil Extracellular Traps (NETs). NETs are structures released by neutrophils in response to certain stimuli, such as infections or inflammation.
  • They are composed of chromatin, which is the DNA of the neutrophil itself, along with histones and various antimicrobial proteins. NETs help to trap and kill microorganisms, particularly bacteria, by immobilizing them and exposing them to these antimicrobial proteins.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 81.

questions.stemHtml: Which type of cell signaling is shown in the figure below ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Paracrine
  • Paracrine signaling is a form of cell communication in which cells secrete signaling molecules that act on nearby target cells.
  • The signaling molecules, known as paracrine factors, are released into the extracellular space and diffuse over short distances to reach neighboring cells.
  • These factors bind to specific receptors on the surface of target cells, initiating a signaling cascade that leads to a cellular response.
  • Example: One example of paracrine signaling is the release of growth factors by cells to stimulate the division and growth of nearby cells. For instance, during tissue repair, platelets release growth factors that promote the proliferation of neighboring cells to aid in the healing process.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 584-585. Inderbir Singh's Textbook of Human Histology- 8th Edition, Page no. 39, Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition Page no. 32.

questions.stem: A patient presented to emergency. ABG is done and report shows pH 7.2, PaCO2 80, HCO3 35. Which of the following acid base disorder it is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Respiratory Acidosis
  • Based on the given arterial blood gas (ABG) values, the patient's pH is 7.2, PaCO2 is 80 mmHg, and HCO3 is 35 mEq/L.
  • In this case, the pH is below the normal range (7.35-7.45), indicating acidemia.
  • The PaCO2 is elevated (greater than 45 mmHg), suggesting respiratory acidosis.
  • The HCO3 is also elevated (greater than 26 mEq/L), which is not consistent with compensation for respiratory acidosis.
  • Therefore, based on the ABG values, the acid-base disorder in this patient is Respiratory Acidosis (option A).


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 322
